articles.title: Evil Dead Burn Is the Most Gruesome Entry Into the Franchise Yet, but It Misfires on Other Essential Elements in Evil Dead's Spellbook
articles.summary: Evil Dead Burn is easily the most violent and oppressive Evil Dead movie yet, and even with the occasional gruesome highs of the horror on screen, this one manages to feel too similar to its predecessors while also leaving out some of the essential elements of Sam Raimi's beloved horror franchise.
articles.body:
Evil Dead Burn opens in theaters July 10.

For as straightforward a conceit as the Evil Dead franchise has traded on for over 40 years – read from the cursed book, awaken the vengeful Deadites – it’s always been something of a magic trick to watch how far each movie can push that conceit while still remaining true to the creative spirit of Sam Raimi’s 1981 original . Raimi’s sequels set some very loose boundaries in that regard, but Fede Alvarez and Lee Cronin ’s later takes each found varying degrees of success adapting the story into a more modern cinematic context. By comparison, Evil Dead Burn, helmed by French director Sébastien Vaniček, doesn’t meaningfully add much to the conversation.

An extended prologue sets Evil Dead Burn squarely in the aftermath of the events of Rise, as a couple of unlucky fishermen find out what happens to those who indulge in outdoor recreation while Deadites are on the prowl. Burn quickly catches up with a new set of characters, led by Alice (Souhelia Racoub), a French ex-pat grappling with the recent death of her abusive husband Will Price (George Pullar) and a set of in-laws who are struggling to find a way forward through all that with Alice. Once the Prices hunker down at the family farm, their connection to the fated Necronomicon comes into focus and, if you can believe it, they come under assault by Deadites who are out to recover an artifact in the family’s possession. Once the action moves to the farm, Evil Dead Burn closely adheres to the familiar “dead by dawn” structure favored by its forerunners.

Organizing the Deadite action that’s to follow around Alice’s inner turmoil is a good instinct, but it’s one which Fede Alvarez’s Evil Dead reboot – the movie Burn most closely aligns with tonally – found much more success in mining. Externalizing how Mia’s drug addiction was destroying herself and her loved ones in the form of the Deadites – a level of thematic specificity that Raimi never had much interest mining with the creatures – led to a strong connection between the horrific violence in that movie and its main character, each benefitting in turn. Evil Dead Rise’s Beth learns she’s pregnant, and immediately has the associated anxiety attacking her in the most closely analogous way possible: through her single-mom sister and her kids. Here, Alice is contending with similarly weighty issues in the aftermath of a terrible marriage, but Evil Dead Burn’s attempts to structure itself around how that complicates Alice’s grief tend to ring hollow. Vaniček and co-writer Florent Bernard’s script routinely shortchanges and obscures the character’s personality, giving Souhelia Racoub very little room to build Alice into more than just a cipher for those in abusive situations.

Overwrought stylistic choices further hamper the cohesion between Evil Dead Burn’s action and thematic efforts. Not only do cutaways to a fight between Alice and Will really stretch to explain why burning and fire become such common motifs in the story as it goes, but brief though they are, these jumps out of the confines of the Price farm hurt the momentum of the Deadites’ onslaught. It’s a minor thing, but it’s emblematic of how Vaniček bumps against other more important pillars of the franchise. The Price family falls neatly into horror archetypes: Will’s brother Joseph (Hunter Doohan), a struggling author, serves as Burn’s primary vehicle for delivering Necronomicon-sourced information; there’s also uptight mom Susan, emotionally repressed and explosively angry dad Edgar, and cognitively declining, yet at times spookily lucid grandma Polly. Archetypes can be useful for keeping a story moving, but in an Evil Dead movie, the Deadites are usually more unsettling when they’re playing against their victim’s personality, so Evil Dead Burn’s supernaturally fueled heightening of the Prices’ character flaws feels a little rote as a result.

But amid all the disgusting Deadite mayhem, an Evil Dead film usually leaves room for a laugh . The franchise has always had a particularly complicated relationship to comedy, since Evil Dead 2 eschewed the original’s intensity with its more mischievous pitch and redefined horror-comedies forever in 1987. Evil Dead Burn does make occasional overtures towards dark humor – particularly through Grandma Polly, who functions here a little like Henrietta in Evil Dead 2 – but Vaniček doesn’t have a great handle on when or how to break the tension by leaning into laughs, especially given the dark subject matter Alice is contending with. One moment where a Deadite is trying to convince Polly that there’s a thief in the house with what amounts to a very conversational “oh, oh yeah, totally” pushes the Deadites a little too far into broad comedy. But Vaniček shows an unmistakable preference for shocking grotesquery throughout Evil Dead Burn, and on that count, he doesn’t disappoint.

Vaniček is particularly good at staging moments of Deadite action in close quarters, especially during one early sequence set in a car attempting to leave the property (never a good idea in Evil Dead). Once all hell breaks loose, every moment is a fight for survival that turns a different part of the car into a weapon. Vaniček can scarcely contain his excitement to get from one gory gag to the next, littering early scenes at the Price farm with loudly telegraphed setups establishing all the pokey, stabby stuff bound to be used to pokey, stabby ends later. Once it comes time for those dominoes to fall, Vaniček seldom resists pushing the metaphorical (and often literal) knife in one or two extra times, even in moments where some could argue he goes too far. Burn’s chaotic carnage does get a little exhausting in the home stretch, especially by the end of a climax that feels too close to that of Alvarez’s Evil Dead to create any room for an original final confrontation. The special effects serving those efforts come out of this somewhat scattershot experience completely blameless, something that seemed a safe bet from the moment a character’s flesh melts off their bones like well-braised short rib after being stepped on in the opening minutes. If there’s a part of the human anatomy you’re sensitive to seeing injured onscreen, Evil Dead Burn’s got one hell of an effed up bingo card for you to fill out.

articles.title: Person Behind Viral AI-Generated Fallout: New York Game Hauls It Offline, Says Bethesda Issued Cease and Desist
articles.summary: The person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game has pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda.
articles.body:
The person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game has pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda.

Earlier this week, a self-styled “AI creative” known as “CHRIS FIRST” on X / Twitter published a video of Fallout: New York, a game built by Claude Opus 5.5 and made playable in a browser. It included quests, companions, dialogue trees, Fallout’s iconic V.A.T.S. combat and even a working Pip-Boy.

Fallout: New York, a full Fallout game you play in your browser, built with Claude Opus 5.5. Quests. Dialogue trees. V.A.T.S. A working Pip-Boy. Zero texture files. Zero sound files. Every building, weapon, face and sound is generated by code. pic.twitter.com/58Vls0mOYx — CHRIS FIRST (@chrisfirst) September 28, 2026

Fallout: New York, a full Fallout game you play in your browser, built with Claude Opus 5.5. Quests. Dialogue trees. V.A.T.S. A working Pip-Boy. Zero texture files. Zero sound files. Every building, weapon, face and sound is generated by code. pic.twitter.com/58Vls0mOYx

The initial video, viewed 3.5 million times on X / Twitter, sparked a debate about the rights and wrongs of CHRIS FIRST’s use of AI, with some calling the game AI slop, and others impressed by the gameplay. As you’d expect, many responded to the video to predict that Bethesda would eventually step in, although CHRIS FIRST seemed somewhat naive to the situation.

“It’s all free and I make 0 money on it,” he tweeted. “I hope they don’t ask me to take it down. I really love Fallout and this was just a fun tech demo. But I should add a quest where you have to serve someone papers, but they keep running away.”

The inevitable now appears to have happened. CHRIS FIRST published an image of what looks like an official cease and desist from Bethesda parent company, ZeniMax Media Inc, which points to trademark infringement for the use of the 'fallout.nyc' domain name, as well as its use of copyrighted material. IGN has asked Microsoft for comment.

CHRIS FIRST, meanwhile, remained defiant in his post even as he confirmed the removal of the game. “Hey, @BethesdaStudios,” they said, “how about you make a Fallout game instead so I don’t have to? Sorry to everyone who enjoyed the game! But the suits got involved and the fun is over.”

No-one is particularly surprised by Bethesda’s action here. “Dude this game was ass and didn’t even look like Fallout,” one person said. “I don’t know why you tried to cash in on their IP lmao. They had every right to C and D you.”

“How about you make some original game instead of copying existing one?” another person suggested. “Like no one saw this coming from a mile away. Ppl can't expect to rip off an IP and not get dmca'd,” another said. One person commented: “Everything ur AI game did was already done before In Fallout just mixed around. No new mechanics or innovation.”

“Wow it’s almost like stealing is bad,” another said. “Not sure what you expected with your AI trash,” one person declared. "I would genuinely rather play Fallout Tactics than this AI generated garbage," another said. "Everyone liked that," Karl Schecht, aka professional 3D and technical artist and YouTuber Kommander Karl, said .

This week has seen a number of viral clips of AI-generated “game-merging mods” in which Minecraft is fused with other famous games in what is a growing and controversial trend. One such video, which shows Minecraft copied into Elden Ring, was viewed 22 million times on X / Twitter.

I put the entire of game minecraft into elden ring as mod. its runs on Mac. pic.twitter.com/CojefjxtLn — Anime Girl Worshiper (@TobynJacobs) September 29, 2026

I put the entire of game minecraft into elden ring as mod. its runs on Mac. pic.twitter.com/CojefjxtLn

This in turn has sparked a significant debate about the legality around AI-generated clones and these “game-merging mods,” with some wondering if publishers will step in to take action or push for guardrails that prevent their creation within the AI models themselves. One person has released an AI-generated Splatoon clone, which some believe Nintendo will take a look at sooner rather than later. Another person merged Mario with Elden Ring.

so long, gay margit pic.twitter.com/pTTodFIq9v — Deltaroo Δ (@Deltaroo3D) September 30, 2026

As the debate over AI-generated games rages on, video game publishers will be desperate to keep a tight leash on their franchises. AI is making what was traditionally a painstaking process of reverse-engineering and recompilation significantly faster, which has prompted some to wonder about the future of commercial video game development. Why buy a Switch 2 if you can have AI generate a clone of one of Nintendo's exclusives? Others, though, have pointed out that none of these game-merging mods or clones display any creativity or present any new ideas, rather take existing popular video games and either mash them together or simply replicate what is already playable better elsewhere.

Bethesda is of course working on a number of official Fallout games, including Fallout 5, Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters, and a spinoff from Fallout: New Vegas developer Obsidian Entertainment. None has a release window, although new Xbox boss Asha Sharma has talked about wanting to double down on the company's biggest franchises, including Fallout.

articles.title: Disney President Reacts to Live-Action Moana Flop, Says It Was an 'Excellent Film' Hit by 'Unusual Circumstances'
articles.summary: Disney president Dana Walden has blamed "unusual circumstances" for the live-action Moana movie's disappointing box office, and defended the project as an otherwise "excellent film."
articles.body:
Disney president Dana Walden has blamed "unusual circumstances" for the live-action Moana movie's disappointing box office, and defended the project as an otherwise "excellent film."

Speaking this week at the Bloomberg Screentime event (via Variety ), Walden framed Moana's poor performance as a result of the movie industry being competitive, and the film simply launching at the wrong time.

"It's so competitive right now that you have to have... the right film at the right time, with audiences feeling a certain degree of demand," Walden stated. "I would say our live-action Moana, which is excellent, I think it was hurt by the proximity to our second animated version of Moana, which came together under unusual circumstances, but premiered about 18 months before this one."

Ranking the Best Live-Action Disney Remakes

The unusual circumstances Walden is referring to here relate to Disney's relatively last-minute pivot that saw Moana 2 change from launching as a Disney+ series to a theatrical movie. This resulted in the project being slotted into Disney's film schedule awkwardly just a year and a half before the long-gestating plans for a live-action film.

"Perhaps there was not enough time to create a lot of pent-up demand for another film," Walden concluded.

While most would agree the timing was indeed awkward, it's fair to point out that this issue is one entirely of Disney's own making. (Perhaps the live-action movie would have performed better if it was held back until a year later, with Moana 2 more of a distant meory?)

But then there's also the matter of the movie's quality. While Walden is unlikely to say anything other than the film being great, the majority of critics disagreed. Moana sits with a 33% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with an average rating of 4.8/10. Pre-release, the film's trailers were also subject to audience criticism over the movie's CGI backgrounds and a slew of memes over Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson's luscious wig .

"Dwayne Johnson returns as Maui opposite newcomer Catherine Laga'aia in this frame-by-frame retelling of the Disney animated musical that doesn't do enough to justify being made," IGN wrote in our live-action Moana review , awarding the movie a 6/10.

While the Moana franchise will continue with a third animated film following the breakout success of Moana 2, there's no word of a live-action sequel being made. You're welcome, indeed.

articles.title: 'I've Buried It Deep': X-Men Actor Says He Knew Sony's Spider-Man Spinoff Kraven Wasn't 'Going Well' During Filming
articles.summary: Marvel's new X-Men movie star Christopher Abbott has admitted that he knew Sony's Spider-Man spinoff Kraven the Hunter wasn't "going well" while on set.
articles.body:
Marvel's new X-Men movie star Christopher Abbott has admitted that he knew Sony's Spider-Man spinoff Kraven the Hunter wasn't "going well" while on set.

The Girls and Catch-22 actor had a small role in Sony's notoriously-bad Kraven movie, and said it was immediately clear that the film had issues. Speaking via the Happy, Sad, Confused podcast, Abbott recalled not knowing what he was doing on set, and basic details of his character being unclear.

"I can s**t talk myself," Abbott began, saying that he was comfortable critiquing his own performance. "I don't know what I was doing in that thing. I didn't understand what the superpower was, I didn't know what was going on.

How to Watch Sony's Spider-Man Universe in Chronological Order

"I was like 'I take off my glasses and what happens?' I feel like no one really had a good answer," he continued. "I don't know what I was wearing in that thing. I've sort of buried it deep down."

Kraven the Hunter was one of Sony's various mediocre Spider-Man Universe spinoffs that the studio pumped out while attempting to establish its own cinematic universe. While the Tom Hardy-starring Venom found success (and gained two sequels of varying quality), Sony also launched the Jared Leto-starring Morbius and Dakota Johnson-starring Madame Web before finally deciding it could not continue.

Various in-development projects were abandoned over the years, including films centered on minor Spider-Man characters such as El Muerto, Jackpot, and Hypno-Hustler. There was also a vague plan to bring these standalone films together via a Sinister Six crossover movie, with groundwork to set this up evident in Morbius' mid-credits scene (which features the MCU's Vulture, played by Michael Keaton) and the post-credits scene of Spider-Man: No Way Home (which features a brief Tom Hardy cameo).

"That was a learning curve," Abbott concluded, reflecting on Kraven the Hunter. "In the moment, I was like... 'I don't think this is going well.'"

"Kraven the Hunter takes aim at the audience and instead shoots itself in the foot with ill-conceived action and a poisonously rote script that totally botches its razor-thin examination of toxic masculinity," we wrote in IGN's Kraven the Hunter review , awarding the film an awful 3/10.

Thankfully, Abbott is being given a fresh crack at the superhero movie genre with a leading role in Jake Schreier's upcoming X-Men reboot. Officially part of the MCU and a key focus for Marvel post-Avengers: Secret Wars, this new version of the X-Men will feature Abbott as Charles Xavier/Professor X, alongside Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Scott Summers/Cyclops and Adam Driver as Nathaniel Milbury /Mr. Sinister. It's a fair bet this will be slightly better than Kraven.

articles.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Star Wars: Galactic Racer from developer Fuse Games very clearly isn't settling for being a run-of-the-mill arcade racer with a flashy license.
articles.body:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer from developer Fuse Games very clearly isn't settling for being a run-of-the-mill arcade racer with a flashy license.

Instead, Galactic Racer sprinkles innovation all over the tried-and-true genre while predictably nailing the gameplay elements better than most genre mates.

Fuse Games might be new, but the fingerprints of great racers are all over Galactic Racer, which makes sense, as senior developers from Criterion Games, of Need for Speed and Burnout fame, are involved here.

It shows, and at launch, it's super obvious other racing games will be scrambling to take inspiration from this brilliant marriage of gameplay and overarching systems.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is gorgeous. It's a modern Burnout with a Star Wars layer of paint that is impossible to ignore.

All the detailing, visual effects and sound design are there, but the general racing game staples like cities and mountains have been replaced with dusty, detailed backwater locales where some of the most interesting Star Wars tales are free to take place. Gone are traditional vehicles in favor of unique Star Wars vehicles and all the odd alien species to boot.

The Burnout DNA is all over this one. Getting aggressive with opponents and sending them off the track into a fireball of carnage gets the beloved slow-mo takedown perspective.

Plus, the sense of speed is nearly unmatched in the genre. It helps that the controls are punchy, the vehicles weighty and the rip-roaring sound design is so immersive.

Galactic Racer adds in that arcade-like feel to each run with a standard turbo boost system, plus another risk-reward boost that lets players flirt with "redlining" an engine. Push that boost too far and the vehicle explodes (though certain perks and builds let players toy with this risk-reward balance in great ways).

Tack on little details that play with the world and track designs, too, like a progressing freezing meter that players can cleanse by steering into a heat vent. Problem is, everyone wants to do that, so there are wrecks to be had at that event, to say the least. Some wrecks feel unfair, given the nature of this Star Wars racer at these speeds, but it's never ruins the experience.

Players select from a handful of vehicle classes:

Like simulation racers, players have a fine control over upgrades, parts, abilities and styles. Much of these are what they sound like: Parts offer passive shakeups to control of a vehicle (and come in different rarities), abilities are actionable on track and the 14 racer styles have unique traits and/or abilities.

It's a lot. And it's a welcome ' a lot .' This game could have easily gone an arcade-racer route with a handful of different-feeling characters and called it a day. Instead, there's a fine layer of player agency in how they navigate each run.

Galactic Racer also goes a really unique route, with the solo campaign actually being a roguelite, or what the game calls "runs-based."

So in that spirit, a run can end with a wreck that scraps a current vehicle build, players can fine-tune the actual risk involved before a run and there are overarching progression systems to improve, even in a loss.

There is, believe it or not, some off-track gameplay here too in the form of little third-person breaks that progress the story. It's another little "they didn't have to do this, yet did" sort of addition that is appreciated.

Player agency is the name of the game, from start to finish. The superb overarching design decisions in these areas are only bolstered by the fantastic-feeling racing itself.

Narratively, Star Wars: Galactic Racer is set after Return of the Jedi, meaning the New Republic Era. That gives the game some serious creative leeway to loop in plenty of deep cuts as characters.

Physically, the tale's Galactic League takes place in the Outer Rim and sees the protagonist, beyond simply trying to win, support Darius Pax against the bad guys.

It's fantastic. The marriage of Star Wars lore and settings with traditional racing-game stuff is so great. This is an unsanctioned league, yet syndicates sponsor racers just like brands would in say, a racing sim like Forza or similar. Contracts from backers offer in-race objectives, too.

And again, this being a sort of roguelite makes the solo campaign have a certain level of replayability. Players pick event paths via a chart, sort of like the route map from say, Slay the Spire.

Customization only adds another layer of player control and replayability, too. Progression-wise, like similarly-designed efforts across roguelite genres, players can still make progress despite defeat. Things like points that purchase vehicles, the styles and even a sort of reputation system carry over between runs.

An arcade mode is the expected time-based sprints with unlocks and a variety of scenario modes like events, time trials and others. Speaking of scenarios, it gets its own mode here. These involve racer styles unlocked via campaign mode, making each longish scenario feel unique to that character.

Online multiplayer for Galactic Racer loops in up to 12 players. There's a general quick race mode, but the real highlight is Multiplayer Tour.

That mode features a six-planet tour in which players earn upgrades and kit out their build over the course of the event before the big finish. Things like backer contracts are there, too, but so are pre-race bets in which a player properly betting on their finish can earn even more rewards.

It's a blast, and the progression of unlocks doesn't hurt either. These multiplayer bits unlock plenty of things like customization options, including new liveries.

Despite the chaos and visual effects at high speeds, Galactic Racer runs well and hits the expected notes, including difficulty settings, in the options menus.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer does the near-impossible: It surpasses the lofty expectations that come with the Star Wars license and overdelivers with surprises atop the usual arcade racer formula.

Talk about innovative, too. Whereas recent racers like Mario Kart have dabbled in the open-world side, Galactic Racer plays the "what if?" game by taking its arcade racer in a Slay the Spire direction.

The results are engrossing. Addictive, even. Truly, the Star Wars window dressing atop the whole thing is just an added bonus. It's nice to have another in-universe hit like this so soon after Star Wars Zero Company, no doubt, but this would have been a hit regardless.

None of this, by the way, mentions the superb balance between pick-up-and-play with competitive depth, too. Star Wars: Galactic Racer is an incredible first lap for the developer and easily on the Game of the Year shortlist.

articles.title: ⚾️ Y! Sports AM: The final eight
articles.summary: Four playoff teams are out. Eight teams remain. It’s on to the Division Series.
articles.body:
Yahoo Sports AM is our daily newsletter that keeps you up to date on all things sports. Sign up here to get it every weekday morning.

The Braves bounced back from a deflating Game 2 loss to defeat the Phillies, 6-2, on Thursday night in Atlanta and eliminate their division rivals , who have now lost four straight winner-take-all games dating back to 1980.

ICYMI: Three shutdown innings from an improbable source, 32-year-old southpaw Ray Kerr, set the tone. Michael Harris II hopped on a first-inning Aaron Nola sinker for a three-run tank, and the rest was epilogue. The Braves now head to Los Angeles, where a familiar foe awaits.

What's next: All four best-of-five Division Series begin on Saturday , with Milwaukee, Tampa Bay, Cleveland and Los Angeles hosting Game 1.

Brewers vs. Padres: Milwaukee's prize for winning a franchise-record 103 games? A date with the hottest team in baseball. But let's not forget who we're talking about here. The Brewers went 15-3 down the stretch themselves, and get to start Jacob Misiorowski twice if the series goes long enough.

Rays vs. Yankees: New York mashes homers and has MLB's second-highest payroll, while Tampa Bay plays small-ball and has the fourth- lowest payroll. One notable similarity between these AL East rivals? They both shove. The Yankees led the majors in ERA (3.24), while the Rays led the majors in WHIP (1.14).

Guardians vs. White Sox: Chicago led the AL Central for most of the summer before Cleveland stole the division with a September surge. Now they'll meet in a series featuring some of MLB's best rookies, including Chicago's Munetaka Murakami (35 HR) and Cleveland's Parker Messick (12-9, 2.56 ERA).

Braves vs. Dodgers: Los Angeles' bid to become baseball's first three-peat champion since the 1998-2000 Yankees begins against a team that gave them fits all season. Atlanta won five of six meetings, but now faces a rested Dodgers rotation featuring Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow.

The Browns are 3-1 and alone atop the AFC North after beating the Steelers, 27-24, on "Thursday Night Football" for their third straight victory . Pittsburgh erased a 14-point deficit and tied the game in the final two minutes, but Deshaun Watson led Cleveland into field-goal range and Andre Szmyt drilled a 56-yarder with 10 seconds left to win it.

For the second consecutive year, the Aces ended the Fever's season — this time with a 94-83 victory in Game 3 to secure their eighth straight trip to the WNBA semifinals. Reigning MVP A'ja Wilson powered the home team with 36 points and 10 rebounds, while Chelsea Gray came alive late to tally 23 points alongside five assists.

Igor Shesterkin beat the Lightning at both ends of the ice on Thursday, stopping 24 of 25 shots and scoring on an empty net to lift the Rangers to a 5-1 win in their home opener. He's just the 18th goaltender in NHL history to score a goal and first to do it for the Rangers. Two games into the season, he's tied for the team lead in goals.

Each week, Yahoo Sports AM goes "Behind the Lens" with Getty Images to share the stories behind the best photographs in sports.

This week's photo: The second wave of runners takes off along the famous Straße des 17. Juni at the start of the Berlin Marathon, as shot from the viewing platform of the Victory Column in the city center.

I usually run the Berlin Marathon myself, so it had been a few years since I photographed it. I was actually quite nervous I wouldn't make it in time, because during the race the city is heavily closed off and the distances between shooting locations can be quite long. So, I packed my gear into my backpack and set off by bike.

First thing in the morning I went to check if the Victory Column was open to have a nice general view of the race. After climbing all 285 steps to the viewing platform I realized it was too high up to photograph the elite athletes, so I came back later and climbed up again for the second wave, which is where this image was taken.

Around 56,000 runners started the 52nd edition of this World Marathon Major, and I wanted to capture the colors of the autumn trees in Tiergarten Park — quite a famous running spot in Berlin. Luckily, a little sunlight broke through at just the right moment, lighting up some of the trees as thousands of runners began their race.

There's something special about watching everyone run past. It brings back memories of standing at that very same starting line myself — when your legs still feel fresh, the excitement is everywhere, and you have no idea how you will feel in the end when you eventually come back to the finish.

Equipment and technique: Maja shot this with a Canon R1 100-300mm and a 145mm lens with f/7.1 at a shutter speed of 1/1600th of a second.

This offseason brought the NHL's greatest riches to its youngest players, resuming a trend that was halted during and after the pandemic.

Youth movement: Four of the top 10 highest-paid players (by average annual value of their contracts) are 22 years old or younger. The average age of those 10 players is 26, comfortably the youngest average of the last decade.

Several young stars signed lucrative extensions this offseason, repeatedly usurping the throne as the NHL's highest-paid players in history. Among those shooting to the top of this season's rankings were Leo Carlsson of the Ducks and the Blackhawks' Connor Bedard.

The list will likely get even younger next year, as the record extension signed this summer by 20-year-old Macklin Celebrini begins.

Not sudden: The shift toward youth appears abrupt. In reality, it's the continuation of a trend that began pre-COVID, when a generation of elite stars like Connor McDavid and Auston Matthews signed lucrative, long-term extensions.

However, the salary cap flattened in the years following the pandemic, forcing the next wave into more modest bridge contracts. With little cap space to replace them, the NHL's incumbent high-earners remained at the top of the pay scale.

The salary cap has returned to strong growth in recent seasons, with continued growth projected into the future. Those increases have allowed teams to resume spending heavily on young talent.

The recent expiry of the league's CBA also created a rush of buzzer-beating big-money extensions, as the maximum number of years decreased from eight to seven under the new CBA.

Growth investment: The league's teams are deeply invested in the next generation of superstars. Now, the NHL has to make them household names.

articles.title: ‘As unhinged & woke as her daughter’ – Reporter shares interaction with A’ja Wilson’s mom
articles.summary: A reporter has claimed to have an “unhinged” encounter with A’ja Wilson’s mother during Game 3. A’ja Wilson’s mom was front and centre at Game 3, holding up...
articles.body:
A reporter has claimed to have an "unhinged" encounter with A'ja Wilson's mother during Game 3 .

A'ja Wilson's mom was front and centre at Game 3, holding up a "love beats hate" sign after all the drama in Game 2.

On the court, Wilson got off scot-free without a suspension and dropped an impressive 36 points and 10 rebounds to send the Fever packing 94-83. She definitely got away with a few physical plays and soft calls in the paint that went her way, but she took full advantage, dominating the floor from start to finish.

However, the controversy didn't involve Wilson directly this time round, it was her mom instead.

Jonny Root shares interaction with A'ja Wilson's mom

OutKick's Jonny Root kicked up a massive storm online, claiming he had a chaotic run-in with A'ja Wilson's mom right after Game 3. He called her "unhinged & woke" just for her response when he asked about that "Love Beats Hate" sign, taking a direct swipe at both her and Wilson.

He said in one tweet on X: 'I had quite the interaction with A'ja Wilson's mom when I calmly & respectfully asked about her "Love Beats Hate" sign after Game 3 vs Fever.

'Hint: You'll understand why her daughter freaks out over a man simply pointing at her.'

In another, he said: 'Can confirm that A'ja Wilson's mom is just as unhinged & woke as her daughter.'

He later posted the video of their exchange, and the back-and-forth went like this:

Jonny: "Can you tell me what your sign means?"

Jonny: "No, I'm reading. I'm interested in what your thought is."

A'ja's mom: "I mean exactly what the sign says."

A'ja's mom: "That's what I mean. Listen to me. That's what I mean."

Jonny: "Do you mean that Indiana Fever fans are hateful? I'm just asking."

Targeting someone's mom like that is a low blow, but it shows where sports discourse is really at these days. The conversation keeps drifting away from top-tier basketball and straight into internet drama, where cheap rage-bait and off-court outrage pull more eyeballs than the actual game.

articles.title: IDW Expands the A Quiet Place Universe With Rising Tides Spinoff
articles.summary: Get an exclusive sneak peak at IDW Dark's A Quiet Place: Rising Tides, a new standalone spinoff set in the popular horror universe.
articles.body:
For fans of good horror comics, there's no better place to turn than the IDW Dark imprint. IDW Dark focuses on both spinoffs of popular movie franchises like Smile and Event Horizon, as well as original stories like Beneath the Trees Where Nobody Sees. Just in time for spooky season, IDW is about to debut a new entry in the A Quiet Place franchise called A Quiet Place: Rising Tides.

Ahead of its November release, IGN can exclusively debut a new preview of A Quiet Place: Rising Tides #1. Check it out in the slideshow gallery below:

A Quiet Place: Rising Tides is written by Declan Shalvey and illustrated by Luke Sparrow and Colin Craker. The series tells a standalone story in this horror universe, so no prior experience with the films or IDW's previous miniseries is needed.

Here's IDW's official summary of A Quiet Place: Rising Tides #1:

When a young woman named Grace tracks her estranged father to a run-down houseboat in the Florida Keys, she expects disappointment, resentment, maybe even closure. Instead, the entire world ends.

Now stranded in the aftermath of the invasion that shattered civilization, she and her sick, aging father cling to survival on the open water—the only space safe from the creatures who attack at the sound of a single breath. But his oxygen is running low, supplies are disappearing quickly, and the deadly predators circling the shoreline are learning fast.

And on top of it all, a hurricane is coming.

A tense, new emotional story begins within the world of the acclaimed A Quiet Place franchise. Declan Shalvey (Moon Knight, Wolverine, Terminator) and Luke Sparrow (Terminator) ask: What would you do when stuck between the choice of sudden death or rising tides?

A Quiet Place: Rising Tides #1 will be released on November 18, with a final order cutoff of October 12. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop.

A Quiet Place: Part III is currently slated for release on July 30, 2027. Director John Krasinski recently confirmed the new and returning cast members for the sequel . The franchise also recently made the jump to games with A Quiet Place: The Road Ahead. You can read IGN's review of the game .

articles.title: The Pocket Advance nearly perfects my favorite Nintendo handheld
articles.summary: Ayaneo’s Konkr Pocket Advance resurrects and upgrades the Game Boy Advance with a larger screen, extra buttons, and more capabilities.
articles.body: Although I count the original Game Boy as one of my first tech obsessions, I still consider Nintendo’s Game Boy Advance to be my favorite console of all time thanks to its more comfortable horizontal design (for my big hands) and its expansive catalog of excellent 32-bit and 16-bit games. Ayaneo isn’t the first company to attempt to modernize the GBA, but its Konkr Pocket Advance does it best. The handheld strikes a near perfect balance between authentically re-creating the GBA’s design while updating its hardware with new controls, a much better screen, and the flexibility of Android at a price that feels like a bargain. As much as I still adore the GBA, I’ve eagerly embraced upgrades to the aging console over the years. First it was the clamshell GBA SP that finally delivered a frontlit screen I could actually see without a lamp over my shoulder, and later it was aftermarket upgrades like a backlit LCD display and a rechargeable battery that vastly improved Nintendo’s original hardware. Two years ago, I eagerly purchased Anbernic’s GBA-inspired RG34XX, but all of those have now been replaced by the Konkr Pocket Advance. It’s my first handheld from Ayaneo, and I’ve been pleasantly surprised to find the hardware feels on par with Nintendo’s. The Pocket Advance is an all-plastic affair but with a satisfying heft thanks to extra internal hardware including a cooling fan for its MediaTek Helio G90T processor and a 4,000mAh battery. I opted for the cheaper $109 version with 3GB of RAM and 32GB of storage, which is expandable with a microSD card, but for $129, you can get 4GB of RAM with 64GB of storage built-in. [Image: The Pocket Advance (left) with its larger screen and extra controls next to an upgraded original Game Boy Advance (right). It’s not an exact copy of the GBA, but the Pocket Advance’s dimensions are close enough to fit all the cases I’ve somehow preserved for the past 25 years. Where Ayaneo’s remake really diverges from the original is with eight additional buttons including X and Y action buttons plus four extra shoulder buttons on the top edge. I’m a big fan of the larger D-pad Ayaneo has included, but some retro gaming purists may not be fans of how soft and squishy the Pocket Advance’s buttons all feel. I’ve had to learn to mash the action buttons just a little harder to ensure presses are always registered, but I don’t necessarily think the button feel is a downside because they’re also satisfyingly quiet. [Image: The D-pad on the Pocket Advance (right) is larger than what the original GBA (left) featured and feels better under my larger thumb. The Pocket Advance’s 3.5-inch LCD touchscreen with a glass cover is an excellent upgrade, but it does cater to GBA games with a 3:2 aspect ratio and a 960x640 resolution allowing them to be perfectly scaled at 4x. (The GBA had a 240x160 screen resolution.) Unless you’re a monster who can tolerate playing games that have been stretched vertically or horizontally to fill a screen, emulating games from other systems will result in letterboxing or pillarboxing on the sides, and potentially some visual artifacts from scaling when the math isn’t perfect. [Image: The Pocket Advance includes a headphone jack and features a small dial for adjusting volume instead of buttons. Most similarly sized and similarly priced handhelds run some variation of Linux. There’s a thriving community of developers creating and porting a large assortment of emulators, games, and apps to Linux, but installing, configuring, customizing and updating software is not always a user-friendly process, especially for novices who may only be familiar with using plug-and-play game carts. The Pocket Advance instead comes with Android 12, and while that version feels a little dated, setting up the handheld will feel a little more familiar to anyone with smartphone experience. [Product: Ayaneo Konkr Pocket Advance | Getting the Pocket Advance up and running was relatively easy thanks in part to Ayaneo’s custom launcher called AYASpace that makes it easier to install various emulators. But the handheld also has access to the Google Play Store, or you can install Android apps or add-ons downloaded directly from a website. I’m a big fan of a clean and simple launcher for Linux handhelds called MinUI, so instead of AYASpace, I installed an alternative Android launcher called Cannoli on the Pocket Advance that brings the same aesthetics with several emulators preinstalled and preconfigured. The flexibility of Android means I can set the Pocket Advance to load Cannoli by default, but I have the option to switch back to AYASpace at any time, or install and jump between multiple alternatives. [Image: Unlike the original GBA (left) and handhelds like the Analogue Pocket, the Pocket Advance (right) isn’t compatible with original game cartridges. When it comes to emulation capabilities, you’ll want to keep your expectations limited to “retro” gaming. The Pocket Advance’s seven-year-old processor is powerful enough to handle many titles from the PS2 and GameCube, but the handheld is better equipped to emulate the PS1 and Sega Dreamcast, and you’ll have the best experience with games from even older consoles like the Super Nintendo and Genesis. An easy-access quick settings menu that slides in from the right lets you quickly customize and reconfigure the handheld including boosting its performance (at the cost of battery life) to handle more intensive games, but another thing preventing the Pocket Advance from playing more modern games is its lack of analog thumbsticks. [Image: On the top edge of the Pocket Advance, you’ll find three pairs of shoulder buttons alongside a power button and an additional one that’s customizable. Performance and compatibility will also vary with native Android games and apps. I’ve had a lot of fun playing through Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder’s Revenge once again, but while the Pocket Advance is a passable way to stream Netflix, I can’t get it to play any Disney Plus content without the app crashing out. [Image: [Image: Anbernic’s $69.99 RG34XX is still cheaper than the Pocket Advance and may seem like a better alternative, but I think Ayaneo’s is absolutely worth the extra $40. It’s a more powerful and capable handheld with a higher-res display, and I much prefer the Pocket Advance’s larger D-pad and shoulder button arrangement. I also find the quality of Anbernic’s hardware to be hit and miss. Similar to what others have reported on Reddit, I’ve experienced intermittent issues with the responsiveness of the RG34XX’s D-pad. I haven’t had the motivation to crack it open to attempt a DIY fix, and with the Pocket Advance now in my collection, it’s doubtful I ever will. [Image: Even with buttons that feel very soft, the Pocket Advance is easily the best GBA clone currently available. The Pocket Advance is one of the best retro handhelds currently available and not just because of its nostalgic retro design. As long as you temper your gaming expectations and won’t be frustrated by what it can’t play, it’s an excellent way to revisit and enjoy games from Nintendo’s earlier handheld era. Photography by Andrew Liszewski / The Verge

articles.title: Citizen: Stardust Is a Gorgeous Throwback to a Golden Age Comics Icon
articles.summary: In what promises to be one of the most interesting new comics of 2027, Oni Press is rebooting Golden Age superhero Stardust the Super Wizard in the surrealist adventure Citizen: Stardust.
articles.body:
Ahead of NYCC 2026, IGN can exclusively reveal one of Oni Press' biggest new projects of 2027. Citizen: Stardust is a new collaboration between Mary Tyler MooreHawk's Dave Baker and Black Hammer's Malachi Ward. This 12-issue, prestige maxi-series offers a surrealist reimagining of classic Golden Age superhero Stardust the Super Wizard.

Check out the slideshow gallery below for an exclusive look at uncolored artwork from the first issue of Citizen: Stardust:

Citizen: Stardust is written by Baker and illustrated by Ward, with colors by Hellboy's Dave Stewart. As mentioned, the series serves as a postmodern overhaul of the character Stardust the Super Wizard, who was originally created by Fletcher Hanks and debuted in 1939's Fantastic Comics #1.

Here's the official summary of the new series:

In 1947, no Hollywood star shined more brightly than Barclay Flagg – the rugged and cocksure leading man better known to an adoring public as STARDUST, post-war America's first and most bankable on-screen superhero. Across dozens of films, serials, and radio shows, he entertained millions in STARDUST's hyper-violent, cinematic spectacles – until an attempted assassination by a crazed fan ended his once-luminous career with a bullet. Twisted by pain, excess, and unfailing ego in the decades since, Flagg's decaying, Los Angeles mansion – and the fallen star within it – have become rotting effigies of their former selves ... until a fortuitous and well-timed invitation arrives unexpectedly on the doorstep.

Barclay Flagg has been invited to join The Institute – an experimental arts retreat dedicated to advancing innovation through radical creativity. It’s here that Barclay Flagg can finally craft the long-gestating STARDUST masterpiece he’s always dreamt of making. He can restore his reputation. He can rekindle his celebrity. He can finally save the day.

With a near-unlimited budget and an obsessive crew of fellow Institute creators dedicated to bringing his vision to life, Flagg is about to discover that some dreams are too good to be true … and that the two-dimensional comic book hero inside him could never, ever be truly locked away. The Golden Age is over. The time of STARDUST shall soon begin.

"The probability of Stardust: The Super-Wizard becoming one of the most bizarre and unique comics to be published in 2027 seems extraordinarily high, to me,” said Baker in a statement. “Malachi Ward and I are bringing a new perspective to the superhero world informed by psychogeography, cult sacrifices, and technology beyond human comprehension. If that doesn't make you want to read it? Just know that there's a cat of nine tails made of human skulls.”

Citizen: Stardust #1 will be released in April 2027. Oni will reveal more about the new series at their NYCC panel, which will be held on Friday, October 9 from 4:30 PM - 5:15 PM ET in North-Room S 406.1.

articles.title: 8 Big October Games We've Already Played if You Want to Know What We Think of Them So Far
articles.summary: October is here, which means the Fall is in full swing, which means some of the biggest games of the year drop this month. We've already played some of the biggest ones, so check out our previews of Phantom Blade Zero, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, Final Fantasy Resonance, and more below.
articles.body:
October is here, which means the Fall is in full swing, which means some of the biggest games of the year drop this month ahead of You Know Who . We've already played some of the biggest ones, so check out our previews of Phantom Blade Zero, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, Final Fantasy Resonance, and more below.

There are three difficulty options to choose from, but even at the default setting that I played at, Phantom Blade Zero is hard, and I loved that about it. It never felt cheap; it just demanded more from me. In just over an hour of play, I was easily ten times the player I was when I started. It’s a feeling of achievement that is reserved for the very best action games on the planet. If the rest is anything like what I played, I feel like there’s a real chance that Phantom Blade 0 might be one of those games. Read our full Phantom Blade Zero preview .

I had an absolute blast with Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse. The art and animation are absolutely gorgeous; combat is fun and dynamic with plenty of room to carve out your own personal playstyle thanks to the variety of weapons, Arcana, and relics; exploration was appropriately rewarding and there were plenty of secrets hidden within the cracked walls of the Parisian streets; and the bosses provided a nice challenge without ever feeling too overwhelming for how early I was in the game. Read our full Castlevania: Belmont's Curse preview .

Resonance has the most impressive use of HD-2D I think I’ve ever seen. It’s absolutely gorgeous, and you can see it from the overworld. It’s the way the clouds pass gently overhead, the way the wind seems to rustle the grass beneath your feet. What’s equally stunning is the way your character’s spite moves through all of this. HD-2D is gorgeous, but it can sometimes look like your character is a little out of place in the world. Not so here. Your character looks distinct, but it always seems like they fit. Read our full Final Fantasy Resonance preview .

Warhammer 40K was always such a natural pairing with what has come to be called the "boomer shooter" – these crunchy, nostalgic celebrations of ‘90s mayhem that take notes from the likes of old-school Doom, Quake, and Rise of the Triad. The original Boltgun was one of those team-ups that seems so obvious in retrospect that I was almost mad I didn't think of it myself. With Boltgun 2, the couple of levels I played show a desire to evolve a bit beyond those templates, though. It still has the look and feel of all the blood-drenched classics, while dialing up the scope and expanding the environments and character roster. Read our full Warhammer 40K: Boltgun 2 preview .

Between the mastery and class skill trees, loot, and stat points to distribute, Emberville already appeals to my love of ARPGs, while its gathering and crafting systems have the potential to appeal to a whole different crowd too, like my wife, who is a fan of cozier games. That could make Emberville one of those rare games that we can both enjoy together when it releases and serve as an introduction to the genres for both sides. Read our full Emberville preview .

I didn't even start my Planet Zoo 2 career from the typical top-down strategy game perspective. Rather, I was placed directly into the world at ground height, allowing me to walk around the lush East African Rift Valley in first-person. While some previous Frontier games like Jurassic World Evolution have included this as a feature, making it the first thing you do before placing any buildings or fussing over graphs literally changed my perspective in a positive way. Read our full Planet Zoo 2 preview .

This series has not changed all that much in 20 years. Each sport used either a single Joy-Con or a split pair of them, relying almost entirely on simple motion controls with the occasional button press. I played 100-pin bowling, returning from the original Wii Sports Resort, where a lone red pin denotes the front of an army of pins to knock down. This was a classic back on the Wii, and I’m glad to see it back after it wasn’t included in 2022’s Nintendo Switch Sports. Read our full Nintendo Switch Spors Resort preview .

While Stupid Never Dies isn’t necessarily a roguelike, it does have some of that DNA in its approach to progression. Each venture into the dungeon has a time limit, and Davy won’t be able to make it all the way to the KOM right away. You keep any loot you collect, but each fresh run resets Davy’s level back down to zero. However, as you progress further you will build an XP multiplier, allowing you to level up faster, and make it deeper on the next attempt. Read our full Stupid Never Dies preview.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Batman, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter Feature in First Trailer for Skydance, the Newly Named Parent Company for a Merged Warner Bros. and Paramount
articles.summary: Once merged, Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones company Warner Bros. will exist alongside Paramount as a sub-brand of Skydance.
articles.body:
Once merged, Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, and Game of Thrones company Warner Bros. will exist alongside Paramount as a sub-brand of Skydance.

The historic film and TV studios are being slapped together by David Ellison and backed by his billionaire dad Larry Ellison in a deal worth $110 billion, following a hostile bid for WB last year and despite various regulatory blocks that have attempted to scupper the deal in the U.S. and abroad. Concern has been raised that the merger may lead to thousands of job losses through corporate consolidation, afford control over a huge chunk of Hollywood to the Ellison family, and in turn risk the independence of news networks such as CNN.

However, opposition to the deal has now largely melted away and, with the merger's completion appearing imminent, Ellison has now confirmed that "Skydance" will be the name of his soon-to-be enormous entertainment empire. The Warner Bros. and Paramount branding will still be kept for their relevant subdivisions.

Indeed, a bombastic new trailer for Skydance has also been revealed, showcasing the vast swath of Warner Bros. and Paramount intellectual property that Skydance will have access to, including the DC Comics, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter franchises.

What once was the peak, is now just the beginning. Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. articles.title: The Miami Heat Will Wear GTA 6-Themed Uniforms in a November Match Against Milwaukee
articles.summary: The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City , and will see the home team donning an “all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court.”

Presumably, this means the team is sponsored by Take-Two and Rockstar Games for a GTA 6 marketing stunt. As they go, this is one of the cooler ones.

The event will take place at the Kaseya Center at 7pm EST/ 4pm PT on November 18, the day before GTA launches. A bunch of fancy crossover merch has also appeared on the Miami Heat store , celebrating Vice City.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Yesterday, the top of the Kaseya Center , home of The Heat, was lit up to usher in the collaboration between Rockstar and Miami’s home team. This followed a lengthy negotiation with local officials over the extent to which Rockstar could use Miami as a base for creative advertising.

GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional recreation of Florida housing its jewel, a virtual recreation of Miami called Vice City. In-game, the Kaseya Center is dubbed the Sahara Arena.

Other studios are taking notice of what Rockstar is doing in the lead-up to launch. Earlier, one of the founders of the studio behind Kingdom Come: Deliverance held up GTA 6’s pricing as a potential turning point for the industry and video game prices in general.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously commented on GTA 6’s price speculation, saying: “Consumers pay for the value that you bring to them, and our job is to charge way way way less of the value delivery.

GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition. The Ultimate Edition, which includes extra in-game content, costs $99.99. GTA 6 releases for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.

articles.title: System Shock 2 Remaster Is Free to Keep on the Epic Games Store Right Now
articles.summary: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster is currently free to claim on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026.
articles.body:
PC players can currently pick up System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster for free on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026. As with all of Epic's weekly freebies, anything you claim during the window stays in your library permanently. You'll need a free Epic Games account to claim System Shock 2, and the game is played through the Epic Games Launcher.

Nightdive Studios, the team behind a string of well-regarded classic revivals such as those for Quake and Star Wars: Dark Forces, released the 25th Anniversary Remaster in June 2025.

The update keeps the original design but modernises how it looks and plays, including the following changes:

Remastered visuals, including cutscenes, character models, and weapon models

Adjustable field of view and ultrawide support

The choice of an O.S.A., Marine, or Navy background to shape your playstyle

The original System Shock 2 launched back in 1999, developed by Looking Glass Studios and Irrational Games, blending together an FPS shooter with the character building of an RPG. You wake from cryosleep aboard the faster-than-light ship Von Braun in the year 2114 with no memory of who you are, and the ship is overrun by hybrid mutants and hostile robots.

Its influence is hard to overstate. Many of the people behind it went on to make the BioShock games, which are often described as a spiritual successor to System Shock 2, and the game's blend of environmental storytelling and player choice has shaped plenty of what has followed. The original title garnered a 9/10 rating when it received an updated review. Now, this Epic Games Store deal offers a free way to revisit one of the most influential games ever made.

If the remaster whets your appetite, Nightdive also released a full remake of the first System Shock on PC in 2023, rebuilt with new HD visuals, updated controls and a revamped hacking system. It's a handy way to explore the series' roots, though System Shock 2 works perfectly well as a standalone adventure – that's currently $11.99 on Steam with a hefty 70% discount during the Autumn Sale .

Epic is also giving away Buried Stars this week, so it's worth heading to the store for both. It's an anime-style visual novel in which a group of contestants on a TV show must survive a mysterious attack. Like System Shock 2, it's available to claim until 8 October, and you can add both games to your library in a couple of clicks.

articles.title: Blair Witch Creators Reveal the Movie’s ‘Spiritual Connection’ to Their New Film and Tease the Franchise’s Upcoming Reboot
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview, the original Blair Witch Project creators discuss their modern found-footage horror, The Influencer Project, and tease the 2027 reboot.
articles.body:
It’s been 27 years since The Blair Witch Project premiered in theaters, and now the team behind the found-footage blockbuster is back with a new movie that’s a modern twist on documentary-style horror.

In The Influencer Project , real-life influencer Chiara King travels to Copenhagen to give her followers an inside look at the “glamorous business of online fame.” But as documentary cameras start filming her every move, a menacing stalker begins closing in and the fictional documentary turns into something that blurs the line between “content and evidence, follower and predator, fact and fiction.”

I sat down for an exclusive interview with producers Gregg Hale and Eduardo Sanchez, who also worked on the original Blair Witch Project (Hale as a producer, Sanchez as a director), to talk about what The Influencer Project owes to Blair Witch and what they can reveal about next year’s Blair Witch Project reboot .

As you can see in the exclusive clip above, cameras are everywhere in The Influencer Project. Chiara is filmed constantly both by herself and the always-present documentary crew, striving to hit 10 million social media followers. I asked Hale and Sanchez if that new format will carry over to the new Blair Witch Project film, which is set to release in 2027.

“If you're setting a found-footage movie in this era, then that's the language that we're living with: social media influencers, vertical video, surveillance cameras, cop body cams,” Sanchez says. “So we don't want to say too much about the new Blair Witch movie. But yeah, I mean eventually if you're making it in this era, you have to play with the toys that are available.”

“But I also think the answer for us as ongoing day-to-day creators, and [in] interacting with Dylan Clark, who's directing the new [Blair Witch], is we don't think about stories in that way,” Hale adds. “It's not like, ‘Oh, what is the language of found footage and how are we going to use that to tell this story?’ It always starts with what is the story and when is the story set and what are the characters doing and how does that affect how it would be seen?”

“It's all based on the time period, you know what I mean?” Sanchez says. “So you got to use the tools that are available to you, and so that's the bottom line.”

Sanchez says that, given today’s always-online culture, the pervasiveness of cameras in The Influencer Project was easier to explain narratively than in The Blair Witch Project.

“ Blair Witch took place in 1994,” Sanchez says. “Heather [Donahue, who starred in that film], had a 16mm film camera because that's what you shot documentaries on back then. And then a Hi8 video camera was just [for] behind the scenes, a cheap [way to] shoot stuff. And we just told them to just shoot everything. It's like, ‘God, there's many reasons why she's continuing to shoot this movie [that had] nothing to do with documenting the Blair Witch mythology.’ And so you cut to nowadays, you don't have to worry about that at all. There are cameras everywhere. It's easier to tell the story.”

In The Influencer Project, we watch as Chiara is stalked by an unknown figure and are fed a constant stream of her millions of followers reacting to her increasingly dire situation. While the central horror of The Blair Witch Project hinged on a literal monster in the dark, The Influencer Project is focused on more grounded terror, examining the nightmares that can come with living your life online, and the audience’s reaction to it.

“There’s always somebody lying in wait ready to either interact with you in a good way or interact with you in a terrible way,” Hale says. “And all that stuff comes directly from Chiara’s experiences as a real influencer where every disgusting, despicable thing that is said in that movie has been said to her. The spiritual connection between The Blair Witch Project and this is in The Blair Witch Project, they chose to go into the woods and there was bad shit in the woods. But now you don't even have to make the choice to enter that wilderness. We’re living in that internet wilderness all the time.”

The Influencer Project is in theaters now.

articles.title: Blizzard Adds Beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' Quest to World of Warcraft: Forever
articles.summary: For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.
articles.body:
For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.

'Kyle's Gone Missing!' was added during the Burning Crusade expansion through a Make-a-Wish campaign in 2007 for Ezra Chatterton , who was diagnosed with brain cancer earlier that year. Chatterton, who went by the in-game name of Ephoenix, voiced the quest-giver, Ahab Wheathoof, and had his dog Kyle added to the game, which players were then tasked with finding. The quest went live in patch 2.1.2 on June 19, 2007, and has been in the game ever since.

Sadly, a little over a year later, in October 2008, Chatterton passed away at the age of 12 . The quest has remained a beloved part of the game ever since, and Chatterton has also been referenced multiple times, with Blizzard re-naming the Elder of Thunderbluff (who shows up during the annual Lunar Festival) after him in Wrath of the Lich King.

But because the quest was added during The Burning Crusade, it's not part of the original game, which meant it wouldn't be in World of Warcraft Forever – even if the zone where the quest takes place is the Tauren starting zone. But, after players asked Blizzard to bring the quest to Forever, it's officially been added.

Blizzard added the patch after players asked for it in the forums, when user Nyaria posted saying, "My Husband was very sad that the Make a Wish Quest involving Kyle wasn’t in Mulgore." They even acknowledged that it doesn't fit the 'Vanilla-only' ethos, but stood by it, saying, "Yes it wasn’t added until TBC, but this is WoW: Forever, we already have new quests added in, and it was a cute little quest, and a Make a Wish addition for a poor kid."

Luckily, shortly after that thread was posted Blizzard community manager Kaivax simply posted: "We're working on it. Stay tuned." The entire rest of the thread is full of players thanking Kaivax and the rest of the Forever team for adding the quest. One player, Ikory, claimed to have been a Make-a-Wish kid who survived and thanked Blizzard in a long post , which they signed off with: "I spent 30 years in crippling pain, with a failing heart, that had to be repaired every few years. I am a survivor. I was that kid who was supposed to die. Now I have a freaken PhD. I lived. Make-A-Wish helped me have hope as a kid. I got my wish. I’m glad Ezra got his wish. Thank you Blizzard for still caring about us Make-A-Wish kids after all these years."

Now, just four days later, the quest is officially live in the World of Warcraft beta, as a part of the October 1 patch .

Johnny Cash, the Blizzard Principal Designer who added the quest, posted on X/Twitter , saying "I had the honor and privilege of bringing "Kyle's Gone Missing!" into WoW: Forever. Ezra Chatterton was an enormous WoW fan, the creator and voice actor behind Ahab Wheathoof, and the creator of Kyle. A tear was shed during this one, my friends. Rest in peace, Ezra."

The quest isn't hard to get to, especially if you start off as a Tauren. Ezra's NPC is in Bloodhoof Village, which is the first town you get to while questing in Mulgore. You can pick up the quest as soon as you hit level 5, and you'll need to hunt down plainstriders (giant ostrich-looking things) until you get Tender Strider Meat, which you will then feed Kyle to get him to return home.

It's nice to see that while Blizzard has been pretty adamant about keeping the spirit of Classic World of Warcraft alive in Forever, it's willing to add a little wiggle room to add beloved pieces of WoW history like this quest. For as much as World of Warcraft has a reputation for gold selling and general toxicity , it's moments like this that remind me just how magical this game is, and how much it means to so many people.

articles.title: Pokémon TCG Reportedly Launching First-Ever Valentine’s Day Set in 2027
articles.summary: Pokémon TCG is reportedly launching its first-ever Valentine's Day box set on January 27, 2027, featuring mini packs and packaging that folds into a classroom mailbox.
articles.body:
The Pokémon Company is intending to launch the franchise's very first dedicated Valentine's Day collection on January 27, 2027, according to a recent report from Pokébeach .

While the Valentine set is yet to be officially confirmed, the leaks reportedly suggest that the "Pokémon TCG Valentine’s Box" will be similar in practice to the popular Trick or Trade Halloween series, rather than a full expansion release like Pokémon TCG's Delta Reign or Chaos Rising expansions.

These seasonal sets typically come in compact foil packs containing three cards, alongside sticker sheets. The Halloween releases were given their own pumpkin-stamped Pikachu, so I'd put good money on the Valentine's version getting some kind of suitably pink Pika stamp.

The Trick or Trade range was originally designed as a way for kids to hand out Pokémon cards while trick-or-treating, effectively giving them a Pokémon-themed alternative to candy. Given how expensive some Halloween sweets have become, perhaps the cards aren't such a bad substitute.

The reported Valentine's Box appears to be taking a similar approach, with the packaging and packs seemingly designed around giving cards to friends or handing them out in the classroom. The box is also apparently designed to fold into a little cardboard mailbox, allowing cards to be handed out to classmates in the same way kids might exchange Valentine's cards at school.

That's a cute idea, although given the current state of the Pokémon TCG market, I'm not entirely convinced every box will make it into the hands of an actual child.

Previous seasonal releases have generally focused on reprinted cards rather than introducing a bunch of new full-art cards, but that hasn't stopped sealed products from holding surprisingly strong secondary-market value. The Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (last seen in 2025), for example, contains 40 mini packs with three cards apiece, and currently has a market value of around $75.99 at TCGplayer.

That makes the potential Valentine's release one to keep an eye on, particularly if it proves to be another limited seasonal product. Previous holiday releases have sold out well ahead of launch, so the real competition could come when preorders eventually open.

Pokémon TCG BOOster Bundle - Trick or Trade

There's also currently no word on which Pokémon will take centre stage in the mini set. My vote would be Enamorus, although Fairy-type Pokémon aren't currently part of the TCG's standard format... Yet.

I’d also love to see Sylveon - its pink color scheme and cute ribbons would be perfect. Plus, it evolves by friendship! Other options could be Audino and Blissey, since both are linked with care and kindness - qualities that suit Valentine's Day well- or even Pikachu in loveheart-themed clothing might also show up.

Sylveon would also be an obvious choice. Its pink colour scheme and ribbons are practically made for Valentine's Day, while the fact that it evolves through friendship feels particularly appropriate. Audino and Blissey could also fit the theme nicely given their associations with care and kindness, while a loveheart-themed Pikachu would hardly come as a surprise.

Sara Heritage is a freelance journalist for IGN, specialising in Pokémon TCG. When she's not gaming, you’ll probably find her building yet another LEGO set she absolutely did not need, or chaining ranked matches in Pokémon Champions.

articles.title: The Steam Autumn Sale for 2026 Is Now Live, and We Found the Best Deals
articles.summary: The Steam Autumn Sale 2026 is officially live. What games are you picking up?
articles.body:
If you've been waiting for the nights to draw in before settling down with a new game, the Steam Autumn Sale is now underway, bringing a week of discounts across the PC storefront.

The sale runs through 10 AM PT on October 8, giving you until then to pick up whatever catches your eye. It's worth keeping that deadline in mind, though, as the Autumn Sale is considerably shorter than Steam's two-week Summer and Winter Sales.

Valve moved the Autumn Sale to early October in 2025, when it ran from September 29 through October 6. Before that, the event was held in late November, and it also coincides with nominations for the annual Steam Awards.

Rather than making you wade through Steam's seemingly endless list of discounted games, we've picked out some of the standout deals below. So, if you're looking for something new to play as the evenings get darker, here's where I'd start.

Let's start with the biggest 2026 releases. Resident Evil Requiem, Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight and 007 First Light are each 30% off on Steam. Capcom's survival horror entry arrived back in February and can be yours for $48,99, while 007 First Light is IO Interactive's take on James Bond.

Requiem garnered a strong 9/10 score when Tristan Ogilvie looked at it back in March , while 007 First Light managed an identical score from Luke Reilly at the end of May . The new Lego Batman is easily the best of the last decade, and a true return to form – for $49 from Steam (or $43.39 from Fanatical), it's a steal. These are three of the sale's heaviest hitters, so they're a good place to start if you've been waiting for a price drop.

If strategy and RPGs are more your thing, there are some great 50% discounts. Endless Legend 2, Amplitude's 4X sequel, has recently reached its 1.0 release after a spell in early access, while Xenonauts 2 is an X-COM-inspired tactics game that also hit 1.0 this year. Solasta 2, a turn-based RPG, is also half price, though it's still in early access, so expect it to keep changing.

There's also plenty for players with friends. Big Walk is 20% off, and it's a cooperative puzzle game that supports up to 12 players and launched less than two months ago. Marathon, Bungie's multiplayer shooter, is 40% off, and Stick it to the Stickman, a September release in which you work your way up an office tower, is 50% off.

That's just the newest games, as you can also snag a range of other big-hitters for more affordable money. For instance, Death Stranding 2: On The Beach , is down to $56 from Steam, although you can save a further $5 by opting for a Fanatical key instead.

If you want a hefty discount, then look no further than Far Cry 6. Okay, it isn't the best Far Cry title in the longstanding series, but for $6, it's surely worth a punt? That's 90% off its $60 RRP, and is worth giving a go in my book.

For those wanting to get stuck into an open-world title in the weeks leading up to GTA 6, then Watch Dogs 2 at just $2.49 is one of my picks. It's the sequel to 2013's Watch Dogs, fixes the weak story and characters of the original title and moves the setting to sunny California. Normally $50, it's an absolute steal for a fun blend of an engaging story, interesting hacking mechanics and more.

An interesting slice-of-life job simulator that's discounted somewhat is Retro Rewind. We've seen a lot of these job simulator games crop up in recent years, and this one sees you operate a video rental store in the 1990s. A new update brings video game rentals soon, so you can be up to speed before it drops. At $14 (down from $20), it feels like an affordable piece of fun.

articles.title: Brand New GTA 6 Screenshots Focus on Lucia and Jason's Relationship
articles.summary: Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason.
articles.body:
Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason.

GTA 6's dynamic criminal duo can be seen in four new images published via Love Magazine , which features an illustration of the couple on its cover, and a black-and-white screenshot of the pair in more casual clothes (Jason in a white vest, jacked arms on show, Lucia in a leopard-print crop top).

Two more images show Lucia and Jason together in the booth of a diner, but sat opposite. Is this the setting of a heist planning session, or are the two about to hold-up the very diner they're sat in? Are they having a date, or an argument about the way their criminal undertakings are going? What looks like a large bag set to be filled with stolen money suggests something is afoot.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

Next up are images of Lucia and Jason in more stylish clothes (well, Jason is in bike leathers), and looking fierce while playing pool in what appears to be a biker bar.

The article also includes further detail from Rockstar senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, who discussed the pair's pursuit of the American Dream. GTA 6 portrays this as the couple seeking the ability to own a house and pay off their various debts, rather than a desire to become billionaires. “If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face,” Humphries said. “Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world.”

"We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other,” game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern told Love. “That’s what we felt made them authentic, and a great team.” Game writer Alexa D’Agostino added: “When you are focusing on writing a fully realised person with their own wants, you’re going to get something perfectly imperfect — with clichés, but also undeniably real.”

Speaking of GTA 6 marketing ramping up, The Miami Heat announced it would be heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks . The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City, and will see the home team donning an "all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court."
