articles.title: James Gunn's DCU Reportedly Safe Following Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger, for Now at Least
articles.summary: DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran will seemingly keep their vision for the DCU alive following the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.
articles.body:
UPDATE October 2, 2026, 12:22 p.m. PT: Skydance's David Ellison reportedly told James Gunn and Peter Safran to "keep doing what you're doing" at a meeting that took place earlier this week.

The Hollywood Reporter 's sources say the two moviemakers are staying right where they are "at least for the foreseeable future" after they had a positive meeting with Ellison yesterday. They were both invited to stay, with one source saying that Ellison asked them to simply "keep doing what you're doing." He also allegedly visited the Man of Tomorrow set in Atlanta earlier this summer.

Who the two DC Studios CEOs will report to in the immediate future, however, is less clear. Deadline also corroborated reports that Gunn and Safran will continue to build out their DCU as the merger is finalized.

ORIGINAL STORY: DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran will seemingly keep their vision for the DCU alive following the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.

Rumors that the two comic book movie executives would be shuffled out amidst the tumultuous merger have swirled for months. Now, as the $110 billion deal comes to a close under its new Skydance banner , it seems Gunn and Safran – as well as the cinematic universe that includes projects like 2025's Superman and Lanterns – are safe.

Puck has reported that both creatives "will be invited to stay on at DC, at least initially" as all the moving pieces come together behind the scenes. What the long-term future holds remains to be seen, but it sounds like more DC movies and shows will continue to fall in line as the DCU navigates its early ups and downs.

Adding weight to the continuation of the current iteration of the DC universe is Gunn himself. After that new Skydance title was announced, the former Marvel director took to Instagram to celebrate the news by sharing its flashy new trailer. Included amongst the cuts of Paramount and Warner Bros. logos are shots from Superman, Robert Pattinson's The Batman, and even the DC logo itself.

"What once was the peak, is now just the beginning," Gunn, echoing the trailer, said in the post's caption.

Gunn and Safran officially took over the DC entertainment business in 2022 and will continue to oversee it – at least through 2027. That's when their contracts are set to expire, and while there are plenty of other projects set to release before then, whether they'll choose to renew under new leadership remains to be seen.

In the meantime, the DCU charges ahead. After Superman started things off with a bang and Supergirl failed to live up expectations , the cinematic universe is just days away from airing the Lanterns Season 1 finale . The Green Lantern introduction series has received praise from critics and fans thanks to strong casting choices in Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre as John Stewart. Next up for this month is a theatrical release in Batman body horror spinoff, Clayface .

Next year, The Last Son of Krypton will find his way to the big screen once again when Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow premieres in July. articles.title: Disney+ Shows and Movies Are Now Headed to Netflix, Including Ice Age and Percy Jackson
articles.summary: Disney plans to license a mix of legacy titles and currently-streaming TV shows to Netflix as part of a new deal between the two firms. In the deal, Netflix will host select Disney content for its 325 million subscribers.
articles.body:
Disney plans to license Ice Age, Percy Jackson and more to Netflix as part of a new deal between the two firms.

In the deal, Netflix will host select Disney+ content for its 325 million subscribers, including a mix of legacy titles and currently streaming TV shows. The nonexclusive deal is designed to help boost interest in contemporary Disney series such as Percy Jackson and the Olympians, which joins Netflix on October 4. The first two seasons will appear on the rival streaming platform ahead of its Disney+ Season 3 premiere on November 20.

All five 20th Century Studios’ Ice Age movies will land on Netflix at the same time as Percy Jackson. Will Trent Seasons 1-4, Shifting Gears Seasons 1-2, and Tracker Seasons 1-3 are also heading to Netflix between November this year and February 2027.

Disney and Make-A-Wish Celebrate Nearly 40 Incredible Kids at Disneyland's Wishes Assemble Event

In 2027, a range of Walt Disney Animation and Pixar movies will also head to Netflix, including Soul, Elio, and Raya and the Last Dragon, along with a selection of complete series such as Felicity, This is Us, Revenge, and Fresh off the Boat. Release dates for these vary by region.

According to the Variety exclusive, this will be a mutually beneficial deal, with Netflix getting more content and Disney getting more eyes on the kind of things it offers outside of its biggest franchise titles (and presumably some cash).

Those franchise titles such as Marvel and Star Wars will remain exclusive to Disney+, keeping its Disney-branded titles as the main selling point of the subscription service. Netflix will also continue to invest in its own content, with original series and animations such as Arcane, The Witcher, and Castlevania keeping subscribers fed.

Netflix recently announced its streaming lineup for October , which includes miniseries East of Eden, Ben Affleck’s Animals, and Josh Hartnett squaring off against a sea beast in Below.

Disney+ has an exciting October coming up too, featuring Marvel’s VisionQuest, horrible (in a good way) horror movie Barbarian, and American Horror Story: 13. With Disney+ and Hulu merging their libraries , there’s more choice than ever over there.

It’s just a shame Disney+ had to increase its pricing again ahead of the next big Marvel drop. It’s a bit of a Thor point. If you can’t afford subscriptions to Netflix and Disney, though, at least you’ll be able to catch some Disney+ stuff on Netflix from October 4.

articles.title: MTG’s Hobbit Cards Are the Closest Thing to Owning Rare Tolkien Memorabilia, and Perfect for Collectors
articles.summary: Here's why Magic: The Gathering’s small-ish Hobbit set somehow surpasses the massive Lord of the Rings crossover for die-hard Tolkien collectors, just one month after its release.
articles.body:
For the second time, and likely the last, Magic: The Gathering has taken players back to Middle-Earth with its The Hobbit set (its fifth of the year, if you can believe it), and it’s been pretty great.

That’s perhaps to be expected since the original book laid out a lot of what we consider fantasy tropes. Dragons, goblins, dwarves, and more are represented here in a smaller set than the Lord of the Rings one, all of which have gone on to inspire Magic cards in their own right.

Still, given how tricky it can be to get some products, there’s a good chance that finding Hobbit items can feel like searching for the Arkenstone in Smaug’s treasure hoard. And yet, it feels like, in a way, that’s kind of the point.

Magic: The Gathering - The Hobbit - Preorders

The Hobbit - Play Booster Box (30 Packs)

The Hobbit - Scene Box - Crack the Plates

The Hobbit - Scene Box - Treasures of Smaug

The Hobbit - Collector Booster Box (12 Packs)

Tolkien Collectors Will Love The Hobbit Set

J.R.R. Tolkien’s influence on the world of fantasy cannot be overstated, and there’s a reason that so many early editions of his works have fetched colossal sums of money.

As an example, back in 2025, a fully signed Lord of the Rings first-edition set sold for around £287,700 (or $337,000). That marks the high point of spending, but it’s not an outlier by any stretch.

An unsigned first edition of the book also sold in 2025 for $250,000, while a collection of manuscripts from the author that includes notes written in Elvish has sold for over $200,000, too.

Naturally, memorabilia sells big, too, notably from Peter Jackson’s iconic movies. Props, costumes, and limited-edition art prints fetch piles of gold to make a covetous dragon blush, and that includes pieces from The Hobbit movies, too.

Of course, those figures are colossal compared to the price of even the most expensive cards in The Hobbit set , but there’s crossover there, too.

Smaug, Wicked Worm (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Bard, King of Dale (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Thorin, Mountain-king (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Thranduil, the Elvenking (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

The Queen of Dale (Showcase) (Surge Foil)

Gandalf, Goblins' Bane (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

The Arkenstone (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Smaug the Magnificent (Showcase) (Surge Foil)

Gleaming Splendor (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Whereas the Lord of the Rings set offered full art cards with a slick border treatment that highlighted the series’ characters across heroes and villains, The Hobbit leans into the series’ literary origins with book cover-inspired designs that carry a “well-read” look that makes them feel unique amongst Magic’s wide-ranging treatment offerings.

This writer was lucky enough to pack Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane and Smaug, Wicked Worm in the treatment, and they’ve almost instantly become two of my favorite Magic cards I own. There’s just something about the way they look textured that makes them feel like the latest in a long line of Tolkien memorabilia.

In fact, I’d go so far as to say that these are my favorite treatments we’ve received in years - and an ideal inclusion for any serious collector.

That doesn’t make it any easier to find the cards, mind…

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: Nacon’s new PS5 controller can mix audio from your phone and console

articles.body: Nacon announced what the company is claiming is the world’s first officially licensed PlayStation 5 controller with a built-in screen for adjusting settings like joystick sensitivity or remapping buttons right on the gamepad. The Revolution 5 Unlimited’s screen can also be used to mix audio from multiple sources so while using a pair of headphones connected to the gamepad with a cable you can listen to music from your phone and sounds from the game you’re playing at the same time. The Revolution 5 Unlimited is available for preorder starting today for $229.99 through Nacon’s online store and is expected to ship sometime later this year. While it’s primarily designed for use with the PS5, the R5U features an asymmetrical stick layout similar to Xbox and Switch gamepads with a pair of drift-resistant tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) thumbsticks. Both sticks can be customized by attaching alternate heads featuring different designs and the controller’s D-pad is swappable. You can use a classic four-way design or switch to an eight-way option that makes it easier to perform combo moves in fighting games. Nacon even lets you adjust how balanced the controller feels with 10, 14, and 16 gram weights that can be inserted into the R5U’s non-slip grips. [Image: The R5U features all of the additional shortcut buttons and adjustable triggers you’d expect in a premium controller. On the top of the controller you’ll find a pair of shoulder buttons, a pair of customizable shortcut buttons, and a pair of triggers with adjustable travel that can be shortened to reduce reaction times in FPS games. There’s four additional customizable shortcut buttons on the back of the controller as well as a button used for quickly switching between multiple saved profiles. [Image: A wireless charging dock is included. The R5U is also compatible with PCs and Android devices and customizing its performance and functionality isn’t limited to its built-in screen. Nacon also offers a mobile app for iOS and Android that expands the customization options to include adjusting the thumbsticks’ response curves, tweaking EQ profiles for the audio sources, and modifying the color of the RGB lighting surrounding the right stick.

articles.title: 4 Things to Focus on Outside Combat in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave
articles.body:
We’re back for a new installment in our The Long Game series, where we break down things you can invest in early in games that will pay off long-term. Today we’re focusing on Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, the huge new installment in the long-running series that takes you to the capital of the Dagdan Empire to be a gladiator in the Heroic Games.

Like its predecessor Three Houses, Fortune’s Weave has a split narrative with multiple protagonists. However, this time around, you don’t have to choose one route. You can follow the stories of Cai, Leda, Dietrich, and Theodora in any order and can switch between them at any time once you reach Dagsion, the central hub city.

As with the rest of the Fire Emblem series, Fortune’s Weave is centered on grid-based strategy combat. But it also features a heavy focus on activities outside of combat, with access to a world map you can traverse between story battles. You can find dungeons, towns, traveling merchants, and skirmishes with roving enemies.

That’s on top of running around the giant city of Dagsion, which is full of shops, activities, and people to meet. It can all be a little overwhelming, especially if you’re new to the series and aren’t sure where to start. So that’s what we’re here to help with. Here are four things outside of combat that you can (and should) start taking advantage of as soon as you can.

Support levels and conversations have long been a staple of the Fire Emblem series, with characters amassing points whenever they fight next to each other or provide healing or support in combat. Fortune’s Weave expands that system and adds new ways to build support outside of combat, which you should take advantage of whenever possible.

The primary way of building support is by eating meals together at the inn, which will be available to all protagonists very early in the game. Three people can eat together at once, and everyone has their own food preferences. The inn menu changes daily, and when you pick your group of three, you can see how they feel about each meal.

The amount of support points everyone gains is based on how much they like the meal, so don’t try to force people to eat stuff they don’t like. Meals are particularly helpful for building support points with people who aren’t actively in your party and are a vital way to convince recruits to join you (more on that in a bit), since you can’t build support with them in combat.

You’ll eventually unlock arena training, where you can assign two fighters to train with each other in a variety of ways. This will boost both fighters’ command of weapons, magic, or movement types, while also giving them support points with each other. Arena training is the most valuable way to prepare characters for more advanced combat classes. Plus, it’s available every week, so don’t forget to come back to Dagsion every once in a while to take advantage of it.

Each protagonist will learn about Renown once they get to Dagsion early in the game, and it’s basically a stat that measures how well known you are in the city. Increasing your Renown adds important boosts at certain thresholds, will make it possible to recruit more characters, and it’s a big part of the central gameplay loop of Fortune’s Weave.

All protagonists can take on subquests given out by people throughout Dagsion, most of which will take you onto the world map to find items or get rid of certain enemies. These subquests each give Renown and all have deadlines, but they’re usually pretty forgiving, so you should have plenty of time to do them all.

Paralogues are the exception to that standard. These are more significant side quests that expand on the stories of individual characters. Fire Emblem veterans will already be familiar with paralogues, but they're handled differently in Fortune's Weave than the rest of the series. You can only start one if you talk to the right character in Dagsion during a set period of time, and the deadlines for paralogues are strict (in the most extreme case, there's one on Dietrich's path you can only get on one specific date).

This can be an issue because you might spend an extended period on the world map and blow right past the cutoff date without even realizing a paralogue was available. You won't receive any in-game notification, you just have to be in Dagsion on the correct dates. Completing a paralogue nets you 20,000 gold, a bunch of Renown, and unlocks recruitment for certain characters, so they're very worthwhile. I don't normally recommend playing with a guide, but this is one area where I think it's a good idea to look up the information beforehand. You need to be aware of the dates when paralogues are available so you can plan accordingly. Luckily, IGN has a full breakdown of their dates across all protagonists.

You can also earn Renown by visiting gods in their temples in Dagsion. This becomes available early in the game, but it can be easy to forget about since you don’t get reminded about it. On the map, there are icons for each god’s temple. You might notice that on some days, one of those icons is yellow, which means that god is there in person and available to visit. If you continue chatting with the same god, they’ll get chummy with you and might reveal some additional information about themselves or lore about the world.

While completing subquests and paralogues is the base way everyone can gain Renown, each protagonist also has an additional one that’s unique to them. Cai’s involves doing more quests, called kindness quests. Dietrich can summon enemies to battle at any time, as well as duel combatants in dungeons to steal their combat arts. Theodora gets resource requests that allow her to trade items you’ve gathered for Renown. And for Leda, remember to check the tavern in Dagsion at the start of each chapter. She’ll have new performance requests in certain cities on the world map, where she can dance to receive thousands of gold and hundreds of Renown at once.

Character levels and class progression are obviously important in Fortune’s Weave, but don’t forget about their equipment. You’ll start with wooden weapons, but the armory will quickly add bronze and iron versions that are significantly more powerful. You should upgrade as soon as you’re able to.

In Chapter 6, regardless of whose path you’re following, you’ll be introduced to the blacksmith. The main one is in Dagsion, but some bigger towns on the world map will have one too. They allow you to spend money and smithing materials to upgrade your weapons, with basic weapons only requiring Smithing Stones and more specialized equipment requiring unique materials.

You can gather these materials on the world map, but the best places to find them are mines. These dungeons have crystal deposits you can smash that will earn you guaranteed smithing materials. As you’d expect, higher level mines will have more unique materials, and you can gather a bunch of them in one trip.

Dungeons will also be filled with boxes and barrels you can smash with an attack, and ones that hold items will have golden sparkles on them. You can get a variety of materials this way, including stones and food.

Food can be used at rest spots in dungeons or feast spots on the world map to restore your health and magic, which is particularly important when you’re planning on staying outside of town for a while. Some quests and recruits will also require particular vegetables, meat, or fish, so try to keep a variety of food items on hand in case you need them.

If you’re playing as Cai, he can also use food as bait to lure out animals to catch and use as mounts. If you use rare food, noted by a blue icon with a sparkle in the corner, you’re more likely to attract rare animals. Just make sure you use the kind of food each animal likes: orniuses like fish, horses and pegasi prefer vegetables, while wild bau like meat.

No matter which protagonist you’re leading, your core group of characters won’t be enough to take on later chapters. You’ll need to add to your ranks by recruiting some of the many characters scattered around Dagsion, but you don’t have to wander aimlessly and hope you run into them. All characters will be noted by dots on the map: an orange dot marks a character you haven’t met yet, a green dot means you’ve spoken to them but haven’t recruited them, and a blue dot means they’re a member of your party. Once you’ve met them, you can also teleport to them directly by selecting them on the third tab of the map.

Recruitment combines much of what we’ve already talked about in this article. All characters require that you have specific support and Renown levels, which you can see when you select them on the map or by clicking the “Character Info” option when you talk to them. Some recruits will also have additional requirements, like paying them money, retrieving a particular item, or completing a paralogue, side quest, or story chapter.

In order to recruit anyone, you first need to give them a gift. Any gift will do for the first one, but after that, you should try to find ones you think they’ll like based on their personal preferences. Doing this will also make it possible to dine with them at the inn, which is how you’ll raise their support level high enough to recruit them. The only support level that matters is the one they have with your current protagonist, so make sure you’re inviting both characters to meals.

Recruits have different requirements for each of the protagonists. Someone who needs 10 Renown to be recruited by Cai might only need 4 Renown to be recruited by Dietrich. Meals and gifts are limited each week, so you don’t want to spread yourself too thin by trying to appeal to too many recruits at once. It’s wise to focus on a select few recruits at a time, then move on to new ones once you’re successful.

New recruitable characters will continually be added as each storyline progresses, including the leaders of squads you defeat during the Heroic Games. So keep an eye on the map in each chapter to see if there are any new orange dots. And just in case this is the kind of thing you worry about: Recruiting a character with one protagonist will not remove them from the pool for other protagonists. So you don’t have to be concerned about leaving later protagonists with nobody to recruit.

There you have it, four things to make sure you get a handle on early in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave. For more coverage of this massive game, check out our review , recruitment guide , and 18 things the game doesn’t tell you .

articles.title: GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms New Details on Sex, Drug Use, Decapitation, and More
articles.summary: GTA 6 has received a rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more.
articles.body:
UPDATE October 2, 2026, 11:39 a.m. PT: PEGI has seemingly updated its website to remove the age rating for GTA 6.

The PEGI 18 page – which, as viewed by IGN, included what appeared to be new details about GTA 6 – is no longer available. In its place is a blank listing that says, "The requested page could not be found." Users on X/Twitter have captured and shared an image of the listing and have continued to share its contents across social media. IGN has reached out to PEGI for comment.

Grand Theft Auto VI PEGI rating is now up! pic.twitter.com/6MhVcAA1xc — iGrandTheftAuto.com (@iGrandTheftAuto) October 2, 2026

Grand Theft Auto VI PEGI rating is now up! pic.twitter.com/6MhVcAA1xc

ORIGINAL STORY: GTA 6 has received an age rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more.

The update, which can be found on the Pan European Game Information board's website , gives players a relatively in-depth description of Rockstar Games' megaton video game ahead of its launch in November. The PEGI 18 rating arrives just one day after GTA 6 received its official ESRB rating , which, also unsurprisingly, resulted in an "M for Mature."

GTA 6's rating describes a story that allows players to take control of "Jason Duval or Lucia Caminos, two criminals who become involved in a criminal conspiracy following a failed robbery." It adds that they'll work together as "they become increasingly entangled in criminal activities" in Vice City, with gameplay that, as we've already seen, is par for the course when it comes to Grand Theft Auto.

What's different about GTA 6 is the unprecedented detail Rockstar has shoved into the game , with previous footage showing off an open-world sandbox with enough activities to make up for the 13-year wait. PEGI dived into that, too, but there are still even more new highlights to go over.

The board described the game's violence as "bloody with a high degree of realism." Some weapons will be more brutal than others, with some said to be "able to cause greater damage, such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment." This time around, Rockstar has made drug use "frequent and prominent," with players able to partake in illicit substances. Cocaine is said to be especially important in Vice City, with the rating promising that Jason and Lucia will be able to use the substance directly from their inventory, as it can be "snorted directly from their hand at any time."

The GTA 6 PEGI description also touched on " strong sexual themes ," which include "nudity, scenes of intercourse, and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes." It's a lot that we knew and some details that we didn't, but you can read the "content specific issues" section of the summary in its entirety below.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

"This game contains frequent depictions of violence; due to the free roam nature of the game the player can harm all other characters inhabiting the environment," PEGI said. "This includes civilians, criminals and the authorities. Violence is bloody with a high degree of realism, with certain weapons being able to cause greater damage such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment.

"Drug use is frequent and prominent with the player being able to partake in drug use with others and to use illegal drugs directly from their inventory. Most notably, cocaine can be carried around by the player and snorted directly from their hand at any time.

"There are also strong sexual themes, including nudity, scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes. In various night clubs the player can also pay for private dances, during which, the game allows the player to move their hands onto the dancers’ breasts and buttocks."

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

The PEGI age rating also mentioned "other issues," including that domestic animals can be harmed, though not in the same detail as humans. The word "f**k" is also featured prominently in the game, while the word "c**t" is only occasionally featured. The description also said that "discriminatory language can be heard in the TV shows and on the radio channels."

Finally, GTA 6 reminds players that they will have the option to purchase in-game items, though it's still unclear what this entails. In August, it was reported that Rockstar would not include microtransactions or generative AI in the game .

GTA 6 is still on course to launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. You can read more about how Rockstar has ramped up its marketing tactics here , and you can see what we learned from some new screenshots here . While we wait for any more updates, you can read IGN's interview and preview .

articles.title: Ex-Rockstar Boss Dan Houser Doesn't Play a Lot of Open-World Games – and Doesn't Plan to Play GTA 6
articles.summary: Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures.
articles.body:
Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures.

"Given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]," he told Variety . I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently."

"It’s not my job within any company that I’ve ever worked at, thankfully, to be the person that understands what everyone else is doing," Houser continued. "I’m trying to think about new ways of doing it. So when we worked on Red Dead Redemption, as soon as we started working, I never watched another Western. I never watched The Sopranos until after I left Rockstar. I saw one episode, because my girlfriend-now-wife and I did watch the finale in real time. I’d not seen any of it before that moment. And then I watched it all during COVID. And I’m grateful. It’s so good that it would have disrupted everything I did on GTA, had I watched at the time. So I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me."

On not playing many other open-world games, Houser said, "I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature.’ I’m not a game designer, I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about."

Houser's new company, Absurd Ventures, is currently working on two games, as discussed in my all-too-brief conversation with him at LA Comic-Con last year. The studio has already released American Caper, a graphic novel series. Its double-sized season-finale issue drops next month – a week before GTA 6 – along with the book "A Better Paradise."

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.body:
DC's latest live action series is wrapping up its first season this weekend. Even if the series makes some interesting departures from the source material, it's safe to say that Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart have charmed both new and existing fans of the Green Lantern.

Amazon happens to be launching its October Prime Day sale next week. In the lead-up to that sale and the Lanterns season finale, the retailer has dropped prices on tons of Green Lantern merch. Quite a few games have now been released for the Switch 2 and some of them require an enormous amount of space. Final Fantasy 14 is the most gigabyte-hungry game to date, requiring about 117GB all by itself. That game alone takes up half of the Switch 2's internal storage capacity. Other plus-sized games include Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade (90GB), Split Fiction (70GB), Cyberpunk 2077 (60GB), and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment (44GB). Nowadays it's completely possible to download just three or four games and find yourself completely out of onboard storage.

articles.title: GTA VI llega a la NBA: los Miami Heat serán Vice City el día antes del lanzamiento del juego
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Miami cambiará su nombre para jugar contra los Milwaukee Bucks
articles.summary: El equipo de Miami cambiará su nombre para jugar contra los Milwaukee Bucks
articles.body: Rockstar sigue con la campaña de promoción de GTA VI. El próximo gran juego de la franquicia, llamado a ser uno de los que marquen un antes y un después en el mundo de los videojuegos, y lo cierto es que el marketing que están llevando a cabo está a la altura. El último paso que han dado es llegar a la mayor liga de baloncesto del mundo: GTA VI estará en la NBA. El próximo 18 de noviembre, el día anterior a la salida de GTA VI, en Miami se vivirá un partido muy especial. Los Miami Heat recibirán en el Kaseya Center a los Milwaukee Bucks, exequipo de su estrella, Giannis Antetokounmpo. Pero no se llamarán Miami Heat, sino Vice City. Así es, Miami Heat ha confirmado que el partido contra los Bucks no será jugado ni con su nombre ni con su equipación de siempre. El equipo se llamará por un día Vice City, el nombre que la ciudad pasa a tener en el juego de Rockstar. Esto no es solo una muestra de la fuerza de Rockstar, capaz de adentrarse en una de las ligas más importantes del planeta por un día, es una de las campañas más grandes de promoción de un videojuego en la historia. Y es que si ya nos parecía increíble que pudieran colocar el letrero de "Welcome to Vice City" en la parte de arriba del estadio de los Heat, nadie podía llegar a imaginar que la desarrolladora llegara a conseguir que el equipo se cambiara el nombre. Leonida es la versión de Florida de GTA VI, y Vice City la forma de representar a Miami. Sin embargo, la propia ciudad abraza el ser una de las localizaciones más recurrentes de los juegos de Rockstar, y del que podría ser, si todo termina siguiendo el camino que se espera, el mejor juego de 2026. Aunque resulte curioso, tenemos un antecedente similar a esto en la G-League, la liga de desarrollo de la NBA. Aunque no llega a la escala de esta colaboración, fue el equipo 'filial' de los Cleveland Cavaliers, llamado Cleveland Charge quien cambió su nombre. Colaborando con el juego Backyard Basketball, el equipo cambió su nombre a Cleveland Melonheads, en su partido contra los Delaware Blue Coats. Es lo más parecido a lo que sucederá el próximo 18 de noviembre, cuando podremos ver a Vice City en la mejor liga de baloncesto.

articles.title: Verity Is a Dismal Colleen Hoover Adaptation Starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, and Josh Hartnett
articles.summary: Verity review: A veritable mess starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, and Josh Hartnett.
articles.body:
In a Guardian piece on how Colleen Hoover became a global best-selling author, one YA fan that was interviewed by the paper suggested it was because she’s “writing for people who don’t like reading.” If that's the case, then one could argue that the film adaptations of her work are for people who don't like cinema.

Now that I've watched all four films inspired by her literary prose — 2024's It Ends with Us, 2025's Regretting You, this year's Reminders of Him, and now Verity — I'm making that case. For these are not adaptations that make any attempt to elevate the middling narratives fumbling around Hoover's novels; I realised this when reading It Ends with Us after suffering through the movie, and I vowed never to read another.

With Verity, I had more hope that it would buck the trend. Divorced from the sentimentality of previous adaptations, this story opens with a meet-cute that’ll give you whiplash. After introducing Anne Hathaway's best-selling author Verity Crawford through interviews with the likes of Gayle King, where she discusses the darkness in her writing, struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh (Dakota Johnson) enters the chat. Lowen's agent has landed her a meeting with Crawford's publishing house for a mysterious job opportunity, but on the way, she not only witnesses a road accident but is drenched in the blood of the cyclist involved. It's an opener as out there as the one in Meet Joe Black (IYKYK), but it does provide an opportunity for Josh Hartnett's handsome stranger to step in and help clean her up.

In typical Hoover fashion, the pair trauma bond: He tells her he dragged his dead daughter out of a lake, and she says her mother died of cancer the week before. There’s no build up, just some awkward exposition-dumping in a men's toilet. They're soon reunited at the publishing house, where it’s revealed that he's Verity's husband, Jeremy. He and the editors want to commission Lowen to finish his wife's novel series; Verity is in a comatose state after a car accident and cannot speak or move. So, with little deliberation and due to the shoehorned fact that Lowen is also being evicted from her New York apartment, she packs up and moves into the Crawfords' sprawling Vermont home for six months.

There she meets Verity, a shell of her glamorous self wearing a glazed stare. This is one of the few scenes the women share; most of Hathaway's performance is marginalised to interviews on the likes of Hot Ones and the Call Her Daddy podcast, as well as flashbacks layered with sultry voiceovers as Lowen reads Verity's secret autobiography. Every time she picks it up, sentences run across the screen, and often Lowen is superimposed over scenes from the past to try to enliven the act of reading. It doesn't.

What's most infuriating is how long it takes Lowen to finish the text. It’s unbelievable that an author would constantly run away from the autobiography to masturbate and go on a date with Jeremy, given how unflinching Verity's candour is. She reveals juicy details about her marriage and hints that their daughter's death might not have been an accident — how did she not finish it in one sitting? Nothing screams “padding for time” more than this tedious set-up, accomplishing little in the way of ingratiating the viewer with Johnson's "pick me" girl protagonist.

Nor does it scratch the surface of who Jeremy actually is beyond the one-dimensional trope of a swoon-worthy husband. Screenwriter Nick Antosca, who recently impressed with his adaptation of Cape Fear, hints at some resentment on Jeremy’s part for his wife's success, but the script never probes deeper than in a final act reveal that flings the missing pieces at you in one blink. The best Antosca offers is an examination of the reliability of the narrator, but even that effort is phoned in. Michael Showalter's direction is similarly dull, conveying little of the vision seen in his Oscar-nominated films, The Eyes of Tammy Faye and The Big Sick. Instead, it plods an uneven, uninspiring route into cliché and lazy convention.

That Anne Hathaway has been on an exquisite run of big screen releases from The Odyssey and Mother Mary to The End of Oak Street and The Devil Wears Prada 2 makes this, her last 2026 performance, even more disappointing. What a lead balloon for everyone involved — one that proves a moratorium on Colleen Hoover adaptations is long overdue. To misquote Lady Catherine from Pride and Prejudice: "Are the shades of cinema to be thus polluted?"

articles.title: A’ja Wilson fan confrontation interrupts Fever-Aces playoff game
articles.summary: A’ja Wilson received a technical foul after confronting Fever fans during Indiana’s 99-89 playoff victory over Las Vegas.
articles.body:
A tense exchange between Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson and spectators drew attention during Indiana's 99-89 playoff victory Tuesday. The incident followed a 4th-quarter foul involving Sophie Cunningham and resulted in a technical foul for Wilson.

Two fans were briefly escorted from their baseline seats before returning after a security review. Indiana said security found no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct.

Playoff game turns heated after late foul

The incident unfolded during Game 2 of the first-round playoff series between the Indiana Fever and Las Vegas Aces at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Indiana faced elimination after losing Game 1 by a 102-85 score. The Fever responded at home with a 99-89 victory.

That result tied the best-of-3 series at 1-1 and forced a deciding Game 3. The confrontation occurred with 4:10 remaining in the 4th quarter and Indiana leading 90-79. Sophie Cunningham was called for a blocking foul involving Wilson as Chelsea Gray drove toward the basket.

After the whistle, Wilson turned her attention toward a spectator positioned near the baseline. The interaction quickly led players and other personnel to move toward Wilson as officials handled the situation.

Wilson approaches baseline during tense fan exchange

Video of the sequence showed a male spectator standing near the baseline and pointing in Wilson's direction. Wilson responded by moving toward the seating area and pointing back. Other people quickly moved between Wilson and the spectator.

Officials assessed Wilson a technical foul following the exchange. She remained in the game and finished the contest with 22 points and 9 rebounds for Las Vegas. Aces coach Becky Hammon later said she was told the technical foul was issued because Wilson stepped off the court.

The penalty did not lead to an ejection. Wilson continued playing as Indiana protected its 4th-quarter advantage. The episode became an additional storyline in a game that already carried major stakes because Indiana needed a victory to keep its postseason run alive.

Fans return after security completes incident review

Two fans were temporarily escorted from their baseline seats during the incident. Arena security spoke with the people involved while reviewing what happened. The fans were later permitted to return to their seats.

The Fever said security investigated a reported comment directed toward a player. Security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses during the review. The team said the investigation found no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct.

The fans were not permanently removed from Gainbridge Fieldhouse. The Fever said it considered the matter closed after security completed its review. No further action against the fans was announced by the team.

Wilson explains what prompted her emotional reaction

Wilson discussed the confrontation after the game and focused on the spectator's actions. She said she saw a man taking steps toward her while pointing at her. Wilson described that behavior as unacceptable.

She said spectators should not approach or point toward players in that manner. Her explanation centered on what she believed she saw and experienced during the interaction near the baseline. Wilson also acknowledged that her response resulted in a technical foul.

She apologized to her teammates for receiving the penalty while explaining why she reacted. Wilson did not provide a detailed account establishing exactly what the spectator said during the exchange. That distinction matters because Indiana's later security review concluded that the reported interaction did not amount to a violation of the arena's Fan Code of Conduct.

Hammon discusses Wilson's unusual response to spectator

Hammon said she did not see exactly what happened at the beginning of the confrontation and mainly witnessed its aftermath. However, she emphasized that Wilson's response was highly unusual based on her experience coaching the Aces star. Hammon has coached Wilson in Las Vegas since 2022 and said she had never previously seen her react in that manner during a game.

Hammon said Wilson appeared to feel deeply disrespected during the interaction. Her comments did not establish exactly what the spectator said or intended. Instead, they provided the coach's perspective on Wilson's reaction.

Hammon's remarks also underscored how unusual she considered the episode. Wilson's own postgame comments focused on the spectator's movements and her belief that the behavior toward her crossed an acceptable boundary.

Cunningham foul precedes baseline confrontation

With 4:10 remaining and Indiana leading 90-79, Sophie Cunningham was called for a blocking foul involving A'ja Wilson. The whistle stopped play near the baseline. The confrontation involving Wilson and a spectator followed during the stoppage.

Video showed a spectator pointing toward Wilson before she approached the baseline and responded. The exchange involved Wilson and spectators seated near the court. Available reporting does not indicate that Cunningham took part in the verbal interaction.

The incident occurred late in the 4th quarter at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Arena security responded after receiving a report about a comment directed toward a player. Security later spoke with the fan involved and witnesses as part of its review.

Fever victory keeps Indiana's playoff run alive

Indiana's victory kept its postseason run alive after the team entered Game 2 facing elimination. Caitlin Clark led the Fever with 27 points, 15 assists and 7 rebounds. Kelsey Mitchell scored 26 points, and Aliyah Boston added 22.

Together, Clark, Mitchell and Boston produced 75 points as Indiana answered its Game 1 loss with a strong offensive performance. The Fever won 99-89 and tied the first-round series at 1-1. Clark's performance played a central role in extending Indiana's season, while Mitchell and Boston supplied major scoring support.

Las Vegas could not close the series on the road despite Wilson finishing with 22 points and 9 rebounds. The result sent both teams back to Nevada for one deciding game.

Indiana and Las Vegas will settle the best-of-3 first-round series in Game 3. The deciding matchup is scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 1, in Las Vegas. The winner will advance to the next round, while the losing team's season will end.

Indiana enters the matchup after extending its season at home, while Las Vegas gets another opportunity on its home court. The fan confrontation added another element to an already intense playoff matchup, but the series remains tied after two games. Indiana responded to its Game 1 defeat with a 10-point victory in Indianapolis.

Las Vegas now has to answer at home. Game 3 will determine which team advances, bringing the focus back to the playoff stakes after the attention surrounding Wilson's 4th-quarter interaction.

Little-known fact: A'ja Wilson was selected No. 1 overall by the Las Vegas Aces in the 2018 WNBA Draft after a standout college career at South Carolina.
